question: Pushyamitra Sunga's capital was at:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pataliputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pushyamitra Sunga, the founder of the Sunga Dynasty, established his capital at **Pataliputra**, which was a significant political and cultural hub in ancient India.
 
• Pataliputra (modern-day Patna) was strategically located near the confluence of the Ganga, Son, and Gandak rivers, making it a center of trade and administration.
 
• Pushyamitra Sunga overthrew the Mauryan Empire in 185 BCE and assumed control, marking a shift in political power.
 
• The city of Pataliputra continued to remain an important administrative center under the Sunga Dynasty.
 
• The Sunga rulers were known for their promotion of Hinduism and revival of Vedic traditions, which flourished in Pataliputra during their reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sunga Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Sunga Dynasty was established by Pushyamitra Sunga after the decline of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• It lasted for approximately 112 years, from 185 BCE to 73 BCE.
 
• The dynasty is known for its contributions to Indian art, architecture, and culture, particularly in the development of the Shunga art style.
 
 
 
• **Pataliputra:**
 
 
• Pataliputra was originally founded by the Magadha ruler Ajatashatru in the 5th century BCE.
 
• It served as the capital for several major dynasties, including the Nandas, Mauryas, Sungas, and Guptas.
 
• The city was an ancient center of learning and housed scholars, including those from Nalanda and Taxila.
 
 
 
• **Pushyamitra Sunga:**
 
 
• He was a Brahmin military general under the Mauryan Emperor Brihadratha before he assassinated him to establish the Sunga Dynasty.
 
• Pushyamitra is known for conducting Ashvamedha Yajnas (horse sacrifices) to assert his authority and revive Vedic practices.
 
• His reign marked the decline of Buddhism and the resurgence of Hinduism in the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Pataliputra:**
 
 
• The city played a crucial role in shaping the political, economic, and cultural history of ancient India.
 
• Its strategic location made it a key center for trade, administration, and military activities.
 
• Pataliputra also witnessed the construction of several architectural marvels, including wooden structures and fortifications.
